request.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a hand-drawn ground magic effect for the Arcane Disassembly Furnace in Don't Starve Together. A new visual design, made entirely from this text; there are no input images.

Create ONE coherent original ground-wave design shown in FOUR successive animation key poses, arranged as a clean 2 by 2 sheet, reading top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right. Each quadrant has exactly the same invisible canvas, ground center and camera. No labels, numbers, arrows, dividing lines or panel borders. Transparent RGBA everywhere outside the painted marks, including the large empty center of each effect. Keep all four effects separated with generous transparent gutters and margins. The output is an animation concept sheet, not a scene or a building drawing.

STYLE: authentic Don't Starve / Don't Starve Together 2D ink-and-paint visual language, compatible with hand-painted world buildings. Strong variable charcoal contours and overlap accents; thinner, sparse interior strokes; purposeful pointed line endings, slight asymmetry and irregular hand-shaped curves. Broad connected color shapes, a few angular painted highlights and selected quiet shadow shapes. Keep the silhouette readable at game scale. Hand drawing must come from the shape rhythm and varied ink, never from noise or dense scratches. Material and color articulation should have the same calm spacing as a bronze-and-stone DST building: broad ochre/chestnut facets, a few long tapered marks, clear cyan facets, large quiet spaces. Do not depict actual chunks of bronze or stone: these are thin magical ink/light impressions on the ground.

BUILDING IDENTITY TRANSLATED INTO MAGIC: the associated furnace has an asymmetric bronze crescent arm, an elongated cyan-white hanging diamond, gray-purple stonework and a restrained octagonal brass front medallion. Echo only the crescent sweep, pointed diamond shapes, warm antique-gold highlights and cool cyan energy in the effect's graphic vocabulary. Do not draw the furnace, a miniature furnace, a medallion object, mechanical hardware, cards or a wand. No previous circle design is to be retained.

NEW DESIGN: an unfolding alchemical seal that visibly UNWEAVES itself as it travels outward. The perimeter is made from several broad, separate, hand-inked crescent-shaped energy strokes, with angular cyan diamond slivers caught at a few tips. Uneven spacing and alternating long/short arcs give it a lively eccentric rhythm. The moving front should feel like curled painted marks being drawn, opening and breaking apart. Within the wave's wake, a few short bent rune-like ink strokes briefly appear, then split into small irregular dust-shaped painted fragments. These are invented abstract marks, not an alphabet. The center stays mostly open so the actual furnace and nearby items will remain readable. Strong negative space; never a filled disc or a solid carpet of texture.

CAMERA: a fixed slightly elevated game-world view of a perfectly flat ground effect; its overall circular footprint is naturally seen as a horizontal ellipse roughly twice as wide as tall. All elements lie on this same ground plane, without upright walls, smoke pillars, levitating objects or vertical flames. Both ellipse center and camera are fixed between panels. The largest ellipse occupies about 82 percent of a quadrant's width. The first pose must visibly occupy much less ground than the third. This is a presentation of ground-effect key poses, not a final packed runtime atlas.

FOUR DISTINCT KEY POSES, with real changes in local shape rather than scaled copies:
1. Gathering: a small footprint, about 40 percent of maximum diameter. A few compact curled cyan/charcoal strokes gather around the open center; tiny diamond-shaped glints are still tucked into the curls. No completed outer ring.
2. Unfolding: about 70 percent of maximum diameter. The curls physically uncurl into longer tapered crescent strokes and move outward. Some diamond slivers visibly turn sideways and split. Fresh short angular marks appear in the interior wake while early marks are already dissolving. Show different arc lengths, tip directions and gaps from pose 1. Preserve approximately the same stroke thickness, rather than enlarging all details.
3. Full reach: maximum diameter. The long crescents spread into a broken but clearly legible circular boundary; their curled tips stretch and open, and a sparse antique-gold edge catches on selected leading arcs. Cyan-white highlights stay small and crisp. A handful of incomplete hooked marks remain inside the perimeter. Gold signals full reach but does not become a continuous metal hoop. No intricate mandala.
4. Release: the same maximum footprint as pose 3, NOT smaller. Each former long crescent is now visibly split into separated tapered scraps and diamond dust marks; several entire arcs have vanished, the interior marks have mostly disappeared, and the remaining scraps still imply outward motion. This final pose must show substantial breakup of the design, not just reduced opacity or an enlarged duplicate.

PALETTE: charcoal/plum ink shadows, muted gray-violet undertones, cyan/teal main energy, a little pale ivory highlight and restrained ochre/gold at full reach. Crisp hand-painted color facets rather than smooth neon light tubes. Use transparency between marks. Any softness must be minimal and local; there is no large luminous haze, radial gradient or white bloom hiding the drawing.

AVOID: plain outline circles; uniformly scaled or rotated copies between poses; multiple concentric perfect rings; vector compass geometry; thin neon wire rings; sci-fi HUD; complex symmetrical mandalas; giant starbursts; 3D rendering; polished bevels; realistic glass shards; fire; thick smoke; clouds; rocks; foliage; a solid ground platform; a baked floor or shadow; paper texture; all-over grain; dense hatching; tiny decorative noise; text; visible checkerboard; opaque background. Produce a coherent and clearly animated NEW hand-drawn visual idea with all four stages fully visible.
